newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-National Mutual says institutions pay A$1.60.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-National Mutual says institutions pay A$1.60.

text.p: Australia's second-biggest insurance company, French-controlled National Mutual Holding Ltd, said on Sunday that the institutional portion of its share market listing had been priced at A$1.60 per share.

The company, which is 51 percent owned by AXA SA, said the offer of 280 million shares, or 16.5 percent of the total issued capital, to local and international institutions had closed over-subscribed, pushing the price above the indicated range of $1.35 to A$1.55 per share.
National Mutual will list on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchanges on October 8.
AXA's controlling stake of 866 million National Mutual shares will not be altered by the listings. It said in the offer documents that its stake would not change for at least the next six months.

The remainder of National Mutual, which ranks behind the Australian Mutual Provident Society in terms of assets and chose to list as part if its demutualisation process, will be held 22.6 percent by former policyholders, who opted for shares rather than a cash-out, and 9.9 percent by the public.
Public investors will pay A$1.50 per share, with 168 million shares set aside for this portion of the total offering.
National Mutual said all public investors who applied for up to 9,000 shares would have their allocation satisfied in full and larger applications would be scaled back.
The company will have the largest shareholder base of any Australasian company, with 403,000 shareholders in Australia and 137,000 in New Zealand, a spokeswoman said.

National Mutual group managing director Geoff Tomlinson said the institutional portion of the offering was split between local and overseas investors and followed a lengthy roadshow in Europe, Asia, and North America. "I think a combination of the turnaround in National Mutual Life in Australia and New Zealand and what I consider to be the excellent prospects for us in Asia, particulary in Hong Kong because of our strong position, was of great interest to institutional investors," he told Reuters.

Tomlinson said AXA, which acquired its 51 percent holding for A$1.08 billion in mid-1995, was a long-term investor in National Mutual. "We are basically the third pillar in the AXA group responsible for developing life insurance and associated fund management business in the Asia-Pacific region," he said.
